prompt: A game world is made of $10^2$ chunks, and every chunk holds $10^3$ blocks. How many blocks are in the whole world?
hint: Each power of ten is just a regular number written in a short way. Change both of them before deciding what to do.

hints.text: Each power of ten is just a regular number written in a short way. Change both of them before deciding what to do.
$10^2 = 100$ chunks and $10^3 = 1{,}000$ blocks in each chunk. Equal groups mean multiplying, so find $100 \times 1{,}000$.
$100 \times 1{,}000 = 100{,}000$, so the whole world has $100{,}000$ blocks.

explanation: Change the powers into regular numbers: $10^2 = 100$ chunks and $10^3 = 1{,}000$ blocks per chunk.
Every chunk holds the same number of blocks, so multiply the two numbers: $100 \times 1{,}000$.
Multiplying by $1{,}000$ puts three zeros on the end of $100$, which gives $100{,}000$ blocks.
The zeros show a shortcut: two zeros and three zeros make five zeros, so the answer is also $10^5$.

alternativeExplanations.title: Add the exponents
steps: That is five tens multiplied together, so $10^5 = 100{,}000$ ✓
